references.text: The Baptist John has already testified that Jesus is the Son of God ([ref:Joh 1:34|John 1:34]). Nathanael's confession confirms this same testimony: "You are the Son of God."
Martha similarly confesses that Jesus is "the Messiah, the Son of God" ([ref:Joh 11:27|John 11:27]), a parallel statement of faith to Nathanael's words.
The entire Gospel of John was written so that readers may believe that Jesus is the Messiah, the Son of God ([ref:Joh 20:31|John 20:31]). Nathanael's confession is an early expression of this faith.
Peter's confession "You are the Messiah, the Son of the living God" ([ref:Matt 16:16|Matthew 16:16]) is a close parallel to Nathanael's confession of Jesus as the Son of God.
The disciples confess Jesus as the Son of God after he walked on water ([ref:Matt 14:33|Matthew 14:33]), a parallel to Nathanael's statement of faith.
Psalm 2 speaks of the Son of God who is appointed king on Zion ([ref:Sal 2:6-7|Psalms 2:6-7]). Nathanael combines exactly these two titles: "Son of God" and "King of Israel."
The prophet Zephaniah speaks that "the Lord, the King of Israel, is with you" ([ref:Sef 3:15|Zephaniah 3:15]). Nathanael confesses Jesus as the King of Israel, fulfilling this prophetic expectation.
The crowd hails Jesus as "King of Israel" at his entry into Jerusalem ([ref:Joh 12:13|John 12:13]), the same title Nathanael uses in his confession.
Jesus confirms to Pilate that he is a king ([ref:Joh 18:37|John 18:37]), which corresponds to Nathanael's confession of him as the King of Israel.
Peter confesses Jesus as "the Holy One of God" ([ref:Joh 6:69|John 6:69]), a Christological statement that aligns with Nathanael's recognition of Jesus' divine identity.
God declares himself to be the King and Redeemer of Israel ([ref:Jes 44:6|Isaiah 44:6]). Nathanael recognizes that this divine kingship over Israel is now represented in Jesus.

Philip tells Nathanael that they have found the one Moses in the Law and the prophets wrote about ([ref:Joh 1:45|John 1:45]). Nathanael's confession in verse 49 is his response after meeting Jesus personally.
Even at the cross, the title "King of Israel" is used for Jesus ([ref:Matt 27:42|Matthew 27:42]). The title that Nathanael uses in faith is here used ironically by his opponents.
